tools.description: Start a saved definition once with a unique idempotency_key. Build pinned workspace sources, clone optional PG template and launch worker-supervised services plus owned Kafka/ES. Returns immediately with run/job; poll service_env_status. warm=true prestarts clean dependency capacity for a matching later start. Disconnects never stop services; TTL/explicit stop does.

tools.name: service_env_status
tools.description: Inspect a run or read a retained evidence id; persistent state, exact source/artifact identities, services, progress, events, expiry and cleanup. id omitted lists only this user’s definitions/runs. Reconciles worker state; unknown outcomes remain explicit rather than starting duplicates.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Show data to the user with a view (embedded in the chat): "json" (collapsible tree), "xml" (pretty), "table" (rows), "list-diff" ({first, last, labels}), "text-diff" ({first, last, labels, format}), or a custom view (view_list). Returns the link; mention it.

tools.name: showcase
tools.description: Service showcase: environment health/builds, passport, editable ports/metadata and retained semantic revisions. With target, also impact and an isolated workspace test/patch. Semantic reads never start a parse. If running, observe with job.

tools.name: site_url
tools.description: The full URL of a site link from the site map (browser_sites), with its <param> placeholders filled in. Then open it with the browser navigate tool.

tools.name: task_run_action
tools.description: Open this principal’s task-owned workspace editor/terminal from any chat, including a story-bound credential. The concrete tool must also be granted. Active worker writes stay locked until paused.

tools.name: task_run_catalog
tools.description: Discover the autonomous web task desk, configured model, available research tools and global publication permission. No model call.

tools.name: task_run_control
tools.description: Steer, pause, resume, stop or explicitly checkpoint a persistent worker. Commands are saved before acknowledgement. resolve records a verified uncertain outcome; it never repeats an effect. A checkpoint retains the previous transcript.

tools.name: task_run_list
tools.description: List this principal’s persistent autonomous tasks across chats, with progress, budgets, waits and next actions. Does not resume work or call a model.

tools.name: task_run_memory
tools.description: Browse, read or edit persistent task memory across chats. Omit path for its searchable file index. Editing requires a paused worker and the exact file revision; scripts remain stored evidence.

tools.name: task_run_start
tools.description: Start a persistent autonomous task from /tasks or tools. Gather Confluence/repository evidence into stable memory; optionally let an admin publish findings to one global context. Continues without an open browser; explicit auto_resume controls restart recovery.

tools.name: task_run_status
tools.description: Read durable task progress and journal after a cursor. detail includes the actual retained model messages and context manifest. No execution or model call.

tools.name: test_context
tools.description: Plan outside-in entry-to-exit tests and Testcontainers/warm-lease setup through real service and internal-library code. Returns chain, fixtures, source, skeleton and integrationPlan with dependency-provider guidance. A class target resolves to public callers; choose among multiple entries. Database/client mocks do not prove SQL, wire or broker behavior. Use flow=false or strategy=unit for intentional class isolation; env supplies real-schema DDL.

tools.name: test_coverage
tools.description: Read dev-tool source and lifecycle test evidence, gaps, source freshness and test files. Execution hits do not prove every assertion.

tools.name: test_data
tools.description: Generate TestData, one helper class in the module's test sources with a valid object for every type at the service's edges: request bodies and path variables of its controllers, payloads of its Kafka listeners and of what it sends, the entities its repositories read (a row as the database holds it: id and defaults set; dictionary entities from their real rows, all rows as a list), what its Feign clients answer. Built through each type's constructor; values from Bean Validation, the database columns the names map to (length, scale, CHECKs, FKs to d_ dictionary tables: a real row), how the code parses strings (Long.parseLong(id): the id as text), names, types. Ids of one concept are one constant (ORDER_ID) so a body, an event and a row agree. Bodies validated with @Valid get <body>Cases(): each constraint broken (false) and the edges that pass (true) for @ParameterizedTest. Also with(obj, "field", value) for variants and json(obj). With env, values come from that environment's synced database. Compile-checked; test_context uses it once it exists.

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Run tests of a workspace using reviewed Node node:test file execution or the JVM build. Select target for actual execution placement/dependencies; env is source-catalog provenance. Fast by default on Maven projects: after one Maven prepare per workspace, only changed sources are compiled and the tests run in one JVM (seconds); mode="build" runs the project's Maven/Gradle (the final check). files=[{path, content|edits}] writes before running, so a try is one call. Every result is kept per test, so workspace_patch can show which tests failed before the fix and pass after it (red-green). coverage=true measures changed production lines/branches with fresh JaCoCo data; workspace_coverage_plan previews scope; workspace_coverage reads remaining gaps. The answer has: each test, its status and time, failures with message and the code parts to work on (the repo frames of the stack trace with the lines around them), compile errors with their lines, and the output tail. With env + db (or ddl_path), the run gets a throwaway Postgres database loaded with the DDL snapshot, passed to Spring as SPRING_DATASOURCE_*. Shown as a view. Takes a while: if it answers "running", call it again with that job id.

tools.name: test_targets
tools.description: List reviewed execution target manifests: actual runner placement, dependency environment/access, deployment revision and effects. local, captured-dev and live-dev are distinct. Source env does not imply remote execution.

tools.name: testdb_capabilities
tools.description: Describe the versioned JSON PostgreSQL lifecycle contract, backend capabilities, portable SQL input format, ownership checks and unsupported schema fidelity. Lets alternative language/storage adapters implement the same operations without importing JavaScript internals.

tools.name: testdb_clone
tools.description: Create clean per-run PostgreSQL copies from an immutable template with one private, non-owner application role and datasource settings. Returns logical database bindings and scratch credentials plus a lease. Idempotency key prevents duplicate allocation after a lost response. No state is shared between runs.

tools.name: testdb_gc
tools.description: Recover expired/abandoned leases and owned setup probes, then prune unleased bases by age/LRU/size/count. Active leases and pinned bases are protected. dryRun previews candidates; cleanup failures are returned and retained for retry.

tools.name: testdb_initialize
tools.description: Label and initialize the configured dedicated scratch PostgreSQL cluster for owned test resources. Refuses any configured environment database as the control database. Checks CREATEDB; PostgreSQL templates additionally require CREATEROLE for private application users. Does not write to environment databases.

tools.name: testdb_lease_inspect
tools.description: Inspect one durable lease independently: owning run, logical database bindings, expiry, lifecycle status and cleanup failures. Passwords are omitted. Resource ownership is rechecked by release and template verification.

tools.name: testdb_lease_renew
tools.description: Retain an active debug/test database lease for a bounded time. Expired resources are reclaimed by explicit GC, never silently reused.

tools.name: testdb_release
tools.description: Release one lease and its private role. Drops only registry-owned databases with matching cluster/database markers. Repeat calls are idempotent; any cleanup failure stays visible for GC retry.

tools.name: testdb_reset
tools.description: Reset a suite/test boundary by replacing the entire lease with fresh private copies, then releasing the old copies. Returns new datasource bindings; reconnect the application. This resets committed/asynchronous writes, unlike transaction rollback.

tools.name: testdb_resources
tools.description: Inspect owned scratch databases, active/expired leases, immutable templates and visible cleanup failures. Does not expose passwords. Prefixes alone never establish ownership.

tools.name: testdb_template_build
tools.description: Verify hashed portable fixture SQL, build one prefilled base per logical database, validate constraints/sanity, ANALYZE, then freeze against connections. Identical fixture/policy/PG compatibility reuses the immutable base; changed inputs get a different key. Initialized scratch cluster only. Modes are snapshot, ordered migrations-empty, or ordered upgrade over a base; SQL comes from the verified fixture, not an implicit migration engine.

tools.name: testdb_template_inspect
tools.description: Inspect one template and its verified table counts, content fingerprints, extension versions, physical size and freeze/ownership status. No live source queries.

tools.name: testdb_template_invalidate
tools.description: Mark a base unusable for new clones with an explicit reason. Existing private run databases remain available until lease release/expiry. GC can remove an unleased invalid base before the same input is rebuilt.

tools.name: testdb_template_list
tools.description: List independently updateable PostgreSQL bases and lease summaries, including readiness, size, input identity and timings. Active leases remain distinct from frozen templates.

tools.name: testdb_template_pin
tools.description: Set retention independently from immutable template content. A pinned base survives normal age/LRU/size garbage collection; unpin explicitly when it may be reclaimed. This does not restore an invalid base.

tools.name: testdb_template_plan
tools.description: Offline preparation plan from a verified portable fixture: input content identity, database sizes/counts, compatibility requirements and exact next stage. No PostgreSQL calls or resource creation. The native template key also includes the actual scratch platform, determined at build time.

tools.name: testdb_template_verify
tools.description: Independently verify ownership and frozen metadata. deep=true makes a temporary private copy and compares schema/data/sequence fingerprints without opening the base. Drift invalidates future clones; active run copies are preserved.

tools.name: tool_contracts
tools.description: Inspect versioned language-neutral transport, knowledge, scenario, collection and resource schemas. Use these contracts and the tool_describe adapter result schema when replacing an implementation or migrating storage. Includes stable public schema URLs.

tools.name: tool_describe
tools.description: Read one enabled tool’s exact schema, required fields and guidance before tool_execute. Grants stay unchanged.

tools.name: tool_execute
tools.description: Call a described tool with exact arguments and normal permissions, validation and tracing. Preserves native views; cannot dispatch discovery recursively.

tools.name: tool_profiles
tools.description: List client tool profiles. Listing changes no exposed names; call tool_execute for a described target. Profiles do not grant permissions.

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description: Find enabled capabilities by action, not an object name. Inspect tool_describe, then call tool_execute. Results can include planning guides; no task runs

tools.name: ui_event
tools.description: Scoped UI/backend event bus. Emit only signals in the current principal/chat; no event executes an API request or refresh. Read bounded events after an opaque reconnect cursor; expired cursors return reset=true. ui.* event names are reserved for backend lifecycle signals.

tools.name: ui_page
tools.description: Create reproducible pages from declarative JSON. Save/open never execute. Shared definitions by default (admins publish); private drafts and all execution results stay principal/chat scoped. Widgets include collections, nested collapsible panels, explicit API action buttons and event notices. action=action explicitly sends the declared API request using the viewer permissions; events never send requests or refresh. Poll run/action with job; job_cancel cancels it.

tools.name: ui_page_data
tools.description: Bounded dashboard reads: service_versions aggregates exact Consul services/replicas and reported versions; pg_routines reads overload-aware procedure/function signatures and definition hashes from an exact database. Normal consul_service/pg_query permissions, rate limits and telemetry apply. Incomplete reads never prove absence.

tools.name: ui_trace
tools.description: Diagram a reproducible UI state through observed API requests, multiple grouped service Joern paths and PostgreSQL procedure/function dependencies to tables/fields. capture=true EXPLICITLY replays UI, including form mutations, and takes its screenshot. Default only joins retained evidence (previous result or exchange_ids); no browser or SQL. Exact retained analyses; no implicit parsing. Compact preview and interactive inline graph. Correct missing paths with ui_trace_edit. Observe job or cancel with job_cancel.

tools.name: ui_trace_edit
tools.description: Manually correct a saved UI diagram with optimistic revision checking. patch replaces only supplied definition fields; omitted fields stay intact, [] removes a binding array. Allows title/description/recipe/services/fields/transports/databases/database_links. Corrections remain declared evidence; observed traffic cannot be rewritten. Rebuild with ui_trace previous=<result id>, capture=false to update the inline graph without replay.

tools.name: ui_trace_list
tools.description: Discover saved UI-to-Postgres diagram recipes in this task. Pass id to read replay steps and exact static bindings; no browser, indexing or SQL is run.

tools.name: ui_trace_save
tools.description: Save a versioned task-private UI-to-database diagram recipe without executing it. recipe={url,steps:[{action:"fill",selector:"[name=email]",value:"{{email}}"},{action:"click",role:"button",name:"Search"}]}. Actions: navigate/fill/click/select/check/press/wait. Credentials are runtime parameters. Reviewed service, transport, database and field bindings retain reasons. Use ui_trace_edit for partial edits.

tools.name: view_get
tools.description: A view's HTML and sample data: start a new view from a similar one.

tools.name: view_list
tools.description: Views that show results: built-in ones and custom ones saved with view_save, each with a description of the data it expects.

tools.name: view_save
tools.description: Save a custom view (a new way to show results, e.g. a chart or a domain-specific card). html is the page body: markup plus a <script> that reads DATA (the shown data) and META (title), and may use helpers: dt.esc, dt.$, dt.json(el, value), dt.table(el, rows), dt.prettyJson, dt.prettyXml, dt.highlightXml, dt.diffLists(a, b), dt.diffLines(a, b), dt.copy(text, btn), dt.title(). Styles from the dt pages apply (card, muted, chip, table). Scripts may load libraries from cdn.jsdelivr.net, cdnjs or unpkg. The page cannot fetch anything: put all it needs in the data. Then show data with show(view=name).

tools.name: who_uses
tools.description: Across all passports and the Postgres usage index: which services consume/produce a Kafka topic, read/write a table, call a database function, expose or call an HTTP path, use an ES index or connect to a database; plus database objects (functions, triggers, views, FKs) using a matching table/function. Substring match. Use it to trace flows between services.

tools.name: workbench_inspect
tools.description: Inspect a node returned by workbench_search: retained file/revision, workspace, script/collection or indexed endpoint with source evidence and available prepared actions. Does not run actions. API base URLs remain an explicit deployment choice.

tools.name: workbench_open
tools.description: Open a clickable explorer to browse ticket notes, files and related checkouts, or a service with scripts/queries, tests, Consul and API actions. Chat shows a retained navigator linking to the authenticated live workbench. Normal tool permissions apply; opening executes no actions.

tools.name: workbench_save
tools.description: Save the prepared tool invocation as a revision-checked action recipe in a task context, optionally linked to a service/repository. Redacts credentials; saved artifacts never execute automatically. Reopen through the interactive workbench.

tools.name: workbench_search
tools.description: Search task/context files, owned workspaces, script collections and indexed service APIs together. Fast retained metadata by default; content=true searches text only in an explicit context/workspace with scan limits. Select a returned node with workbench_inspect or workbench_open. No execution or network calls.

tools.name: workflow_plan
tools.description: Inspect a named composable workflow planning guide, or list guide ids. Stages reference exact enabled tools, prerequisites and proof boundaries. A guide never diagnoses a symptom, executes work or grants permissions.

tools.name: workflow_share
tools.description: Named shared workflow definitions: list/get preview immutable revisions; admins publish an exact saved script with referenced scripts and inherited hooks. import copies into a new private collection without executing. Named links contain no task or results. Review embedded code; resolve dynamic script references. Returns compact metadata unless get include_definitions=true.

tools.name: workspace_branch
tools.description: Open/reuse a separate owned workspace at a branch/ref of this repository. Leaves all uncommitted files in the original workspace untouched. Does not push, reset or clean either checkout.

tools.name: workspace_branches
tools.description: List retained branch choices for an owned workspace. refresh=true explicitly reads remote refs (30s timeout). No checkout or source edits.

tools.name: workspace_coverage
tools.description: Read retained change coverage: uncovered changed lines/branches, unknown mappings, exact source/base pins and freshness. This is workspace JVM coverage, separate from dev-tool test_coverage. A stale report cannot claim full coverage; covered lines do not prove assertions.

tools.name: workspace_coverage_plan
tools.description: Plan added/modified JVM production lines against the workspace base commit (or an exact base), including untracked files. No old project coverage baseline is needed. Lines become executable/missed/unknown only after measurement.

tools.name: workspace_delete
tools.description: Delete one workspace file, including temporary progress notes or obsolete source. Pass expected_revision from workspace_read/workspace_write. Marks the code index dirty; tracked deletions appear in workspace_patch. No directories, symlinks, .git changes, commits or pushes.

tools.name: workspace_drop
tools.description: Delete a workspace (its files, git data and index). Take the patch first.

tools.name: workspace_editor
tools.description: Offline workspace editor: list owned workspaces, page folders or search file paths (next_cursor), read UTF-8 text with a revision, save with expected_revision CAS. UI: /editor?workspace=<id>&path=<file>&line=<n>. No implicit compile fixes or external writes.

tools.name: workspace_list
tools.description: Retained workspaces in this authenticated task: id, repo, ref, commit, last use and whether files still exist. Another chat/task scope has its own list.

tools.name: workspace_open
tools.description: Open/reuse a writable repo/ref checkout in the current authenticated task. Reconnects and restarts preserve its files and build state; reuse never pulls or resets. fresh=true creates a separate checkout. Different principals/tasks remain isolated. Indexed for code_search, impact and test_context. Edit with workspace_write, run test_run, export workspace_patch; workspace_push publishes only when requested and enabled.

tools.name: workspace_patch
tools.description: Export workspace changes against its base commit as a downloadable Git patch, file counts and recorded test proof. Does not commit, push or run tests. Use workspace_push only when publishing is requested.

tools.name: workspace_push
tools.description: Commit workspace changes and push to a feature branch only when requested and push.enabled=true. Never force or target protected/default branches. Replays onto a moved branch; conflicts stop the push. Reports recorded test proof but does not run tests or enforce green. Success advances the workspace base to the pushed commit.

tools.name: workspace_read
tools.description: Read copyable workspace source with its line range, or list a folder. line_numbers=true adds display prefixes; never copy those prefixes into workspace_write content. Prefer exact find/replace edits for small fixes.

tools.name: workspace_terminal
tools.description: Bounded, cancellable task-owned command terminal. Fixed inspection commands by default. Builds require an explicit allow_build plus administrator policy and authenticated runner; never accepts shell syntax, custom executables, options, or environment. read polls a job, clear hides prior terminal output.

tools.name: workspace_write
tools.description: Write a file in a workspace: the whole content (new test files), or edits [{find, replace}] where each find matches exactly once (fixes in existing code). The change shows up in workspace_patch. A Java file is compiled right away against its module's classpath: the answer has compile.errors with their lines, compile.fixed (what was fixed in the file already: missing imports and static imports, throws Exception on tests, @MockBean/@MockitoBean for this Spring Boot, javax -> jakarta) and compile.suggestions (ready edits to choose from, e.g. which of several classes to import). Ambiguous imports are suggestions only, ranked with project and configured internal packages first, with reasons. Read compile before the next step; a file with errors does not need a test run to find them. check=false skips the check; fix=false checks but leaves the file as written (the fixes come as suggestions).
